Definition: from G303 and G1080; to beget or (by extension) bear (again):--beget, (bear) X (again).
BiblicalUsage: Peter uses the word twice, and both times it is the new birth: God 'hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,' and we are 'born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.' It is not a fresh start we manage for ourselves — it is a begetting, a second birth, and God is the one who does it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe being born again is the hinge of the whole Christian life: my first birth gave me Adam's nature, and my second birth gives me Christ's life. The hope is lively because the resurrection is real, and the seed is incorruptible because it is God's own word — so the new life in me cannot rot the way the old one did.
